open.heard: 11.47pm, 200 notifications, a release that ships tomorrow and a promise.

promise.heard: 6 o'clock, front row, her daughter's very first piano recital.

habit.heard: Problem is, Dana does everything herself. Every branch. Every review. Every failing test.

scale.heard: But more than 180 million developers build on GitHub, and GitHub has seen this night before.

reveal.heard: So they built the GitHub Copilot app, a desktop home for your coding agents.

mywork.heard: Every session, issue, and pull request from every repo in one calm place.

handoff.heard: Dana hands one small bug to an agent. Just one. Very, very carefully.

models.heard: She picks the model for the job, or lets auto-decide

lanes.heard: Each agent gets its own git worktree, so nobody steps on anybody's toes.

merge.heard: Then, Agent Merge watches the tests, keeps an eye on reviewers, fixes what breaks, and merges when her rules are met.

sandbox.heard: Every agent works in a sandbox, on her laptop or in the cloud.

control.heard: In the cloud, it asks before every change, and autopilot, that's her call.

ships.heard: and the team behind it ships fast. Eight new features in the first 19 days.

listen.heard: and developers can join the discussion right in GitHub Community.

payoff.heard: 6.02 PM, front row, and the release merged at 4.

cta.heard: the GitHub Copilot app. Let your agents do the work. Keep your evenings.
